hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Representative Magic Red images from three independent experiments showed reduced lysosomal cathepsin-dependent proteolysis in APOE4 versus APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding quote: We found that the HsAPOE4-expressing cells exhibited significantly decreased MR-CTSB proteolysis compared to HsAPOE3-expressing cells, in line with their decreased lysosomal acidity (Figure 1F,G).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal cathepsin B substrate cleavage)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing genomic human APOE3 or APOE4; live-cell Magic Red Cathepsin B fluorescence microscopy.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent differentiations, APOE4 human iPSC-derived neurons had lower LAMP1-proximal LGALS3BP PLA signal than isogenic APOE3 neurons.
rows.Finding quote: In concordance with our observations in Neuro-2a cells, we found that APOE4 iPSC-derived neurons harbored less lysosomal LGALS3BP and more lysosomal TMED5 compared to their APOE3 counterparts (Figure 6B,C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal LGALS3BP PLA signal)
rows.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 iPSCs and isogenic APOE3 iPSCs differentiated into mixed neuronal cultures including GABAergic interneurons; DIV49; LAMP1-LGALS3BP proximity ligation assay.

rows.Finding description: FCCP increased the acidic mtKeima response in both genotypes, but the response was stronger in APOE3 than APOE4 cells across three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: While FCCP triggered mitophagy in both HsAPOE3- and HsAPOE4-expressing cells, its induction was stronger in the HsAPOE3-expressing cells (Figure 1I,J).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (weaker FCCP-induced acidic mitochondrial mtKeima response)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and mtKeima; 10 µM FCCP; legend specifies one-hour treatment, whereas Methods specify 30 minutes before imaging; genotype-normalized ratios.

rows.Finding description: Adding bafilomycin A1 to FCCP abrogated the APOE3-versus-APOE4 mtKeima difference across three independent experiments; a comparison-specific significance value was not reported.
rows.Finding quote: While BafA1 as expected reduced the acidic mtKeima signal, it intriguingly also abrogated the difference between HsAPOE3- and HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Figure 1I), suggesting that mitophagic defects could be attributed to defective lysosomal acidification.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, FCCP plus BafA1) -> (no change in acidic mitochondrial mtKeima signal)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and mtKeima; combined 10 µM FCCP and 200 nM bafilomycin A1; three independent imaging experiments.

rows.Finding description: Conventional immunofluorescence across three independent experiments found no observable APOE4-versus-APOE3 difference in LGALS3BP intensity within CTSD-positive human neuronal lysosomes.
rows.Finding quote: While we could not observe differences in lysosomal LGALS3BP localization by this approach (Fig. S6B-C), we could observe a slight increase in lysosomal TMED5 immunoreactivity and colocalization (Fig. S6D-E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LGALS3BP intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 and isogenic APOE3 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; LGALS3BP and CTSD immunofluorescence; lysosomal LGALS3BP intensity; five images from three independent experiments.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, APOE4 human neurons showed a slight increase in TMED5 immunoreactivity within CTSD-positive lysosomes relative to APOE3 neurons.
rows.Finding quote: While we could not observe differences in lysosomal LGALS3BP localization by this approach (Fig. S6B-C), we could observe a slight increase in lysosomal TMED5 immunoreactivity and colocalization (Fig. S6D-E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (slightly higher TMED5 intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 and isogenic APOE3 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; TMED5 intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes; five images from three independent experiments.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, APOE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells had significantly lower LysoTracker staining than APOE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: We found that the LysoTracker intensity was significantly reduced in HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Figure 1A,B), suggesting either endolysosomal alkalinization or a reduction in endolysosomal density.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower acidic-endolysosomal LysoTracker signal)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells carrying the human APOE3 or APOE4 genomic locus; endogenous mouse Apoe intact; live-cell LysoTracker assay, 30-minute loading.

rows.Finding description: Basal mtKeima measurements across three independent experiments indicated modestly impaired mitophagy in APOE4 versus APOE3 Neuro-2a cells.
rows.Finding quote: Under basal conditions, we observed a modest impairment of mitophagy in HsAPOE4 cells (Figure 1H).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower basal acidic mitochondrial mtKeima signal)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and transient mtKeima; basal live-cell ratiometric imaging; individual mitochondria sampled across three experiments.

rows.Finding description: LC3 immunoblotting contributed to the finding that autophagy remained generally functional while basal autophagy was slightly dampened in APOE4 cells.
rows.Finding quote: Autophagy appeared generally functional in these cells, despite the basal autophagy being slightly dampened in HsAPOE4 cells (Fig. S1D-F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (slightly dampened basal autophagy with generally retained autophagic function)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; representative LC3-I and LC3-II western blot.

rows.Finding description: Both APOE3 and APOE4 Neuro-2a cells showed lysosome-autophagosome fusion after three hours of starvation and bafilomycin treatment; no quantitative genotype difference was reported.
rows.Finding quote: Immunofluorescence of LAMP1 and LC3 shows lysosome-autophagosome fusion in both HsAPOE3 and HsAPOE4 Neuro-2a cells following 3 h HBSS starvation and BafA1 treatment.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lysosome-autophagosome fusion remains observable)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; three-hour HBSS starvation and bafilomycin A1 treatment; LAMP1 and LC3 immunofluorescence.

rows.Finding description: LAMP1 immunostaining showed that lysosomal density was not decreased in APOE4 relative to APOE3 Neuro-2a cells.
rows.Finding quote: We therefore stained the cells for the lysosomal membrane marker LAMP1, finding that the lysosomal density was not decreased in HsAPOE4 cells (Fig. S1B-C).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no decrease in LAMP1-based lysosomal density)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; LAMP1 immunofluorescence and Fiji puncta identification.

rows.Finding description: Lysosome-targeted calcium-sensor imaging across three independent experiments found comparable lysosomal calcium levels in APOE3 and APOE4 cells, without a reported significant difference.
rows.Finding quote: Using GPN to release lysosomal calcium [61], we found lysosomal calcium levels to be comparable between HsAPOE3 and HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Fig. S1G-L), particularly after correcting for lysosomal density (Fig. S1M).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in estimated lysosomal calcium levels)
rows.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; LAMP2-GCaMP6s sensor expressed for 48 hours; calcium-free bath; sequential 200 µM GPN and 4 µM ionomycin.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Young APOE4 mice had significantly more hippocampal neuronal lysosomal compartments than APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: Furthermore, while both neuronal EE’s and LE’s showed an increasing pattern with APOE genotype, only N-LY’s showed a significant upregulation in APOE4 (APOE2<E4;E3<E4).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (higher neuronal LAMP1-compartment abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; LAMP1 objects within NeuN soma per neuronal volume; no direct degradation, pH, enzyme-activity, or flux assay.

rows.Finding description: Young cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-dependent change in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: At the same time, N-LE-Ch levels showed similar expression to N-LE’s, while N-LY-Ch levels did not show an APOE dependent change.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young cortex) -> (no change in neuronal lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed neocortex; neuronal D4H* spots overlapping LAMP1, normalized to neuronal D4H* spots and NeuN volume.

rows.Finding description: Young hippocampal neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol and total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-genotype differences in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: There was also a decrease in T-LE-Ch in APOE3<E2, with no change in APOE4, and N-LE-Ch levels were not affected. Similar to the cortex, there was no effect of APOE genotype on total or neuronal LY-Ch, even though neuronal LY levels were increased, indicating that this upregulation is not linked to the LY capacity to process cholesterol.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (no change in neuronal late-endosomal or total/neuronal lysosomal cholesterol reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE knock-in mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; D4H*–CD63 or D4H*–LAMP1 colocalization fractions normalized to DAPI nuclei or NeuN volume; no direct processing-capacity assay.
rows.Data location: Fig 4E, neuronal late-endosomal and total/neuronal lysosomal cholesterol

rows.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-genotype difference in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: There was a striking decrease in both total and neuronal EE-Ch and LE-Ch (APOE4<E2), while there was a complete absence of APOE effect on LY-Ch levels (Fig. 4F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total and neuronal D4H*–LAMP1 colocalization fractions normalized to nuclei or neuronal volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 4F, total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol

rows.Finding description: Young female APOE4 mice had significantly higher hippocampal total late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization than young female APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: Total LE-Ch was decreased in APOE3 females compared to APOE2 and APOE4, as well as APOE3 males.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young females) -> (higher hippocampal total late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; total D4H* spots colocalized with CD63 divided by total D4H* spots and DAPI nuclei; cholesterol accumulation/egress inferred from static localization.
rows.Data location: Fig 9D, total late-endosomal cholesterol, young females

rows.Finding description: Female APOE4 mice had significantly higher cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol than female APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype/age group, but the reporting sentence does not identify the age group.
rows.Finding quote: The only significant difference measured on N-LY-Ch levels was in the APOE4 females, which showed a significant increase compared to APOE2 and APOE3 females, and APOE4 males in the cortex (Fig. 10B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, females, age unspecified) -> (higher cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice; Fig 10 spans 5–6, middle-aged, and 24–26-month groups, but this sentence omits age; fixed neocortex; neuronal D4H*–LAMP1 colocalization fraction divided by NeuN volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 10B, neuronal lysosomal cholesterol; age cannot be assigned from the reporting sentence

rows.Finding description: Young hippocampal total late-endosome and lysosome abundance showed no significant APOE-genotype effect, and neuronal late-endosome increases were not significant, in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: In the HIPP, the total levels of EE’s, LE’s, and LY’s were not affected by APOE genotype (Fig. 4B). Furthermore, while both neuronal EE’s and LE’s showed an increasing pattern with APOE genotype, only N-LY’s showed a significant upregulation in APOE4 (APOE2<E4;E3<E4).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (no change in total late-endosome/lysosome or neuronal late-endosome abundance reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; total CD63/LAMP1 objects per DAPI nucleus and neuronal CD63 spots per NeuN volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 4B, total CD63/LAMP1 and neuronal CD63 measurements

rows.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal lysosome abundance showed no significant APOE-genotype difference in five mice per sex/genotype group.
rows.Finding quote: Both total and neuronal LE’s were decreased in APOE4<E2, while lysosomes were not affected by APOE genotype.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in lysosome abundance reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total LAMP1 objects per DAPI nucleus and neuronal LAMP1 objects per NeuN volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 4C, total and neuronal LAMP1 measurements

rows.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol were qualitatively lower in APOE4 than intermediate APOE3 levels in five mice per sex/genotype group, while the stated significant contrast was APOE4 versus APOE2.
rows.Finding quote: The largest effect was observed in the young EC, with neuronal LE’s, EE’s, as well as total/neuronal EE-Ch and LE-Ch decreasing in APOE4<APOE2 (while APOE3 levels were in between).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (qualitatively lower total and neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE knock-in mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total and neuronal D4H*–CD63 colocalization fractions divided by DAPI nuclei or NeuN volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 4F; Discussion, APOE genotype effects at young age

rows.Finding description: Female APOE4 mice had significantly greater entorhinal neuronal lysosome abundance than female APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype/age group, with ages pooled.
rows.Finding quote: However, paired contrasts showed that N-LY’s in the EC were increased in APOE4 female compared to male mice, and compared to APOE3 females.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, females) -> (higher entorhinal neuronal LAMP1-compartment abundance)
rows.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice from young, middle-aged, and old groups; age-adjusted pooled analysis; fixed entorhinal cortex; neuronal LAMP1 objects per NeuN volume.
rows.Data location: Fig 7C, entorhinal neuronal lysosomes, female APOE4 versus APOE3

rows.Finding description: Entorhinal total and neuronal late-endosome abundance showed no significant three-way interaction or pairwise differences across sex, age, and APOE genotype in five mice per sex/genotype/age group.
rows.Finding quote: In the EC, there were no significant three-way interactions observed affecting CD63 LE levels, and no pairwise differences were detected (Fig. 9E).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, sex- and age-stratified entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in late-endosome abundance reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, three ages; fixed entorhinal cortex; total CD63 spots per DAPI nucleus and neuronal CD63 spots per NeuN volume.

rows.Finding description: Entorhinal total lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant differences in the sex-, age-, and APOE-stratified analysis of five mice per sex/genotype/age group.
rows.Finding quote: There were no differences in total LY-Ch levels in the EC (Fig. 10F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in total lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
rows.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, three ages; fixed entorhinal cortex; total D4H* spots overlapping LAMP1 divided by total D4H* spots and DAPI nuclei.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: Quantification showed greater Apoer2 recycling impairment with ApoE4 than the smaller ApoE3-associated impairment in three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: As shown in Figure 4D and E, physiological concentrations of ApoE3 (5 µg/ml) also impaired Apoer2 recycling to a small, but significant extent. This was also prevented by EMD87580 at the same concentration (3 µM) at which the effect of ApoE4 on Apoer2 recycling was completely neutralized (Figure 4D,E), suggesting that ApoE3 also, although to a minor extent, may lose solubility upon entering the early endosome, and that this is also prevented by pH lowering.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater reduction of surface-to-total Apoer2)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; human ApoE3 or ApoE4 plus Reelin, without EMD87580; surface/total Apoer2 quantification.

rows.Finding description: Quantification of the Apoer2-Fc pull-down showed similar binding of human ApoE3 and ApoE4, with no significant difference reported.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3 and ApoE4 bind Apoer2 with similar affinity, whereas ApoE2 binding to Apoer2 is poor.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in Apoer2 binding reported)
rows.Experimental system: Quantification of the cell-free human ApoE pull-down by mouse Apoer2-Fc; HEK293-secreted ApoE particles at 0–10 µg/ml, incubated with receptor-bearing beads for 4 h at 4°C; immunoblot endpoint.

rows.Finding description: Quantification showed comparable surface-to-total Lrp1 ratios under ApoE3 and ApoE4 across three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: Other ApoE receptors, such as low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (Lrp1) and low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr), as well as the endocytic receptor for transferrin (TfR) and insulin receptor (IR) exhibit comparable surface levels in the presence of ApoE3 or ApoE4.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (comparable surface-to-total Lrp1 ratios)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; human ApoE3 or ApoE4 and Reelin; quantitative surface-biotinylation immunoblot assay for Lrp1.

rows.Finding description: Increasing EMD87580 concentrations progressively restored surface Apoer2 in ApoE4-treated neurons in three independent experiments. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because the experiment holds APOE4 fixed and manipulates NHE6/endosomal pH, a mediator rather than APOE genotype or isoform, so it tests mediation of the receptor-recycling defect, not A itself.
rows.Finding quote: Increasing concentrations progressively restored normal surface recycling of Apoer2 in the presence of ApoE4 (Figure 4B,C).
rows.Finding summary: (increased NHE inhibition with apoE4 present) -> (restored Apoer2 surface recycling)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; EMD87580 pretreatment for 1 h, followed by human cell-secreted ApoE4 and Reelin; EMD87580 dose series; surface biotinylation and surface/total Apoer2 quantification. EMD87580 is not NHE6-specific.

rows.Finding description: Increasing bafilomycin concentrations counteracted EMD87580-mediated Apoer2 recycling rescue in ApoE4-treated neurons across three independent experiments. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because APOE4 is held fixed and the proton pump and NHE are inhibited pharmacologically, which tests whether endosomal pH mediates the recycling defect rather than perturbing APOE genotype or isoform.
rows.Finding quote: Figure 4F and G show that the resulting increase of the endosomal pH reverses the correction of the ApoE4 recycling deficit by EMD87580 and results in renewed impairment of Apoer2 trafficking.
rows.Finding summary: (proton-pump inhibition with apoE4 and EMD87580 present) -> (renewed Apoer2 recycling impairment)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; human ApoE4 and Reelin, EMD87580 3 µM, and increasing bafilomycin concentrations; drugs preincubated before ApoE/Reelin; surface-biotinylation Apoer2 assay. Endosomal pH was mechanistically inferred, not directly measured in this panel.

rows.Finding description: Quantification showed lower surface-to-total Apoer2 after ApoE4 addition than without ApoE4 in three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE-conditioned media treatment reduces the surface expression of Apoer2 in presence of Reelin in primary neurons.
rows.Finding summary: (no added apoE4 -> added apoE4) -> (lower surface-to-total Apoer2 ratio)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; untreated drug-control comparison within the EMD87580 dose experiment; human cell-secreted ApoE4 and Reelin; surface/total Apoer2 immunoblot quantification.

rows.Finding description: NHE6 shRNA a restored surface GluN2B in ApoE4-treated neurons in three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: EMD87580 and the NHE6-specific shRNAs completely restored Apoer2 and glutamate receptor surface expression, while the scrambled shRNA had no effect (Panel B and quantified in Panels C-F).
rows.Finding summary: (NHE6 knockdown with apoE4 present) -> (restored surface GluN2B)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons; lentiviral shNHE6 a/TRCN0000068828, assay 3 days after infection; human ApoE4 and Reelin; surface-biotinylation GluN2B quantification against the ApoE4-impaired control.

rows.Finding description: EMD87580 restored surface GluA2/3 in ApoE4-treated neurons in three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: EMD87580 and the NHE6-specific shRNAs completely restored Apoer2 and glutamate receptor surface expression, while the scrambled shRNA had no effect (Panel B and quantified in Panels C-F).
rows.Finding summary: (NHE inhibition with apoE4 present) -> (restored surface GluA2/3)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons, DIV9–14; EMD87580 3 µM, standard 1 h pretreatment; human ApoE4 plus Reelin; surface/total GluA2/3 quantification corresponding to Fig 6B lanes 2 versus 3.

rows.Finding description: NHE6 shRNA a restored surface GluA2/3 in ApoE4-treated neurons in three independent experiments.
rows.Finding quote: EMD87580 and the NHE6-specific shRNAs completely restored Apoer2 and glutamate receptor surface expression, while the scrambled shRNA had no effect (Panel B and quantified in Panels C-F).
rows.Finding summary: (NHE6 knockdown with apoE4 present) -> (restored surface GluA2/3)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons; lentiviral shNHE6 a/TRCN0000068828, assay 3 days after infection; human ApoE4 and Reelin; surface/total GluA2/3 quantification against the ApoE4-impaired control.

rows.Finding description: NHE5 knockdown left surface Apoer2 low in ApoE4-treated neurons across three independent experiments. Class 5 (other): Class 5 because APOE4 is held fixed and NHE5 is knocked down as a pathway control, which does not act on APOE genotype or isoform.
rows.Finding quote: None of the shRNAs directed against NHE1, 5, 7, 8 or 9 had any effect on surface Apoer2 expression, neither in the absence of ApoE4 or in its presence.
rows.Finding summary: (NHE5 knockdown with apoE4 present) -> (no change in surface Apoer2)
rows.Experimental system: Primary E18 Sprague-Dawley rat cortical neurons; lentiviral NHE5 shRNA, assay 3 days after infection; human ApoE4 plus Reelin; surface-biotinylation Apoer2 quantification.
rows.Data location: Fig 5D; supplementary file elife-40048-fig5-data1.xlsx, sheet Fig5D, E4+R versus E4+R+shNHE5

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: In the NH4Cl-confirmation experiments, Aβ-treated apoE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells had about fivefold greater cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity than Aβ-treated apoE3-expressing cells.
rows.Finding quote: In apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells, A1–42 increased cytosolic -hexosaminidase activity by about 5-fold com- pared with values in A-treated Neo- and apoE3-transfected cells.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
rows.Experimental system: Human apoE3- or apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; Aβ1–42 challenge; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity in the text-only NH4Cl confirmation experiment.
rows.Data location: Results, Low pH Required for ApoE4 Potentiation: sentence beginning 'In apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells'

rows.Finding description: Raising lysosomal pH with NH4Cl reduced Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage in apoE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells to the range observed in Aβ-treated Neo controls.
rows.Finding quote: NH4Cl treatment of the apoE4-transfected cells decreased lysosomal leakage induced by A1–42 to the range seen for A1–42-treated Neo- transfected cells.
rows.Finding summary: (NH4Cl in apoE4 cells) -> (less Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
rows.Experimental system: Human apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; 5 mM NH4Cl for 8 h to raise lysosomal pH; Aβ1–42 challenge; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity.
rows.Data location: Results, Low pH Required for ApoE4 Potentiation: sentence beginning 'NH4Cl treatment of the apoE4-transfected cells'

rows.Finding description: LRP siRNA strongly reduced apoE4 potentiation of Aβ-induced lysosomal β-hexosaminidase leakage in Neuro-2a cells.
rows.Finding quote: Notably, LRP siRNA very significantly reduced apoE4 potentiation of A-in- duced lysosomal leakage (Fig. 11B).
rows.Finding summary: (LRP knockdown in apoE4 cells) -> (less Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
rows.Experimental system: Human apoE4-expressing mouse Neuro-2a cells; LRP siRNA at 1.5 μg/ml with Lipofectamine; 20 μM Aβ1–42 added 48 h after transfection; assay at 72 h; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase.

rows.Finding description: Aβ-treated apoE3- and apoE4-expressing cells showed similar fourfold increases in LAMP1 labeling, with no significant difference between isoforms reported.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE3- and apoE4-transfected cells treated with A1–42 had a similar 4-fold increase in immunocytochemical labeling in the cells.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in reported Aβ-induced LAMP1-labeling response)
rows.Experimental system: Human apoE3/apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; 20 μM Aβ for 0, 8, or 16 h; LAMP1 immunofluorescence images. The fourfold increases are within-group responses, not an E4/E3 ratio.
rows.Data location: Fig 12C, quantification of the staining illustrated in Fig 12B; Discussion, page 9

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: In fibrillar Aβ-challenged APOE4/4 iMG, 10 μM GNE-317 reversed lysosomal accumulation measured by LysoTracker staining in three replicate wells per condition while also reducing lipid droplet accumulation.
rows.Finding quote: In addition, PI3K inhibition with GNE-317 reversed the lysosomal accumulation and inflammatory cytokine secretion observed in iMGs with high concentrations of LDs (Extended Data Fig. 7e,f).
rows.Finding summary: (GNE-317 treatment in fAβ-challenged APOE4/4 iMG) -> (reduced LysoTracker-defined lysosomal accumulation)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; untreated, 5 μM Aβ-treated, and Aβ plus 10 μM GNE-317 conditions over 24 h; the relevant rescue comparison is Aβ plus GNE-317 versus Aβ alone; LysoTracker staining.

rows.Finding description: Lipid droplet-containing APOE4/4 iMG showed greater lysosomal accumulation. Fig. 3s measured the percentage of LysoTracker-positive iMG among cells with and without lipid droplets, using three replicate wells per condition.
rows.Finding quote: In accordance with these RNA-seq results, phenotypic measurements of LD-containing APOE4/4 iMGs indicate that they are dysfunctional in phagocytosis, accumulate lysosomes and secrete inflammation-associated chemokines as measured in the cell culture media (Fig. 3r,s and Extended Data Fig. 6f,g,i).
rows.Finding summary: A greater percentage of lipid droplet-positive APOE4/4 iMG were LysoTracker-positive than lipid droplet-negative iMG.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia in the fibrillar Aβ assay. Fig. 3s groups cells by lipid droplet presence or absence. The live-imaging protocol specifies 5 μM fibrillar Aβ for 24 h before staining.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: ApoE4 increased colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 proximity-ligation signals with Rab11-positive recycling endosomes relative to apoE3, measured in 38 cells per condition.
rows.Finding quote: Altered sorting of sortilin–FABP7 complexes in the presence of apoE4 was confirmed quantitatively by colocalization studies documenting trapping of PLA signals for sortilin and FABP7 in early endosomes (marked by Rab5; Fig. 7F,H) and recycling endosomes (marked by Rab11; Fig. 7G,I) in the presence of apoE4 as compared with apoE3.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater recycling-endosomal colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 complexes)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-K1-derived Chinese hamster ovary cells stably overexpressing mouse sortilin and Myc-tagged mouse FABP7 (CHO-S/F), treated for 24 h with HEK293-conditioned medium containing 5 µg/ml human apoE3 or apoE4. Proximity-ligation signals were co-stained for Rab11; blinded single-z-plane analysis used thresholded Manders’ coefficient tM1. The experiment was replicated three times. These are non-neural hamster cells, not human brain cells.

rows.Finding description: ApoE4 increased colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 proximity-ligation signals with Rab5-positive early endosomes relative to apoE3, measured in 33 apoE4-treated and 34 apoE3-treated cells.
rows.Finding quote: Altered sorting of sortilin–FABP7 complexes in the presence of apoE4 was confirmed quantitatively by colocalization studies documenting trapping of PLA signals for sortilin and FABP7 in early endosomes (marked by Rab5; Fig. 7F,H) and recycling endosomes (marked by Rab11; Fig. 7G,I) in the presence of apoE4 as compared with apoE3.
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater early-endosomal colocalization of sortilin–FABP7 complexes)
rows.Experimental system: CHO-K1-derived Chinese hamster ovary cells stably overexpressing mouse sortilin and Myc-tagged mouse FABP7 (CHO-S/F), treated for 24 h with HEK293-conditioned medium containing 5 µg/ml human apoE3 or apoE4. Proximity-ligation signals were co-stained for Rab5; blinded single-z-plane analysis used thresholded Manders’ coefficient tM1. The experiment was replicated three times. These are non-neural hamster cells, not human brain cells.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

rows.Finding description: Adding the PPAR-γ inhibitor GW9662 abolished the Lilrb4a-knockdown-associated enhancement of Aβ uptake and degradation in APOE4 mouse microglia, with n=3 and replicate identity unspecified.
rows.Finding quote: In both APOE3 and APOE4‐derived microglia, Lilrb4a knockdown enhanced Aβ phagocytosis and degradation, whereas PPAR‐γ inhibition abolished the enhancement of Aβ phagocytosis and degradation induced by Lilrb4a knockdown (Figure 4L–O).
rows.Finding summary: (Lilrb4a ASO -> Lilrb4a ASO plus PPAR-γ inhibition in APOE4 microglia) -> (loss of enhanced Aβ uptake and degradation)
rows.Experimental system: Primary cortical CD11b-enriched microglia from 12-month-old human APOE4 knock-in mice given intraperitoneal LPS, 3 mg/kg, 24 hours before isolation. Ex vivo ASO-L4a plus GW9662 was compared with ASO-L4a alone; ASO dose was 5 pmol per 10,000 cells and GW9662 concentration was 10 µM. Uptake assays used 36-hour ASO pretreatment followed by 24 hours with the indicated PPAR treatment, a 6-hour LPS challenge, and 1.5-hour FAM-Aβ uptake. Degradation assays used 3-hour FAM-Aβ loading followed by 24 hours in substrate-free medium with the indicated ASO and inhibitor treatments; flow cytometry measured residual intracellular fluorescence. Lipid composition, lysosomal pH, and lysosomal enzyme activity were not measured.
